title: The PR's core acceptance metric (top-2% saturation ceiling >= 0.85) has no durable test — one-off python heredoc, nothing in CI
evidence:
The audit's metric: **HSL saturation, mean of the top-2% pixels** ("top-2%
saturation ceiling"). Reproduced to ±0.004 on the audit's own stills
(juice-30000: 0.571 vs audit 0.570; juice-65000: 0.825 vs 0.825;
terminal_types-05000: 0.574 vs 0.572) with
`python3 - <<EOF` + PIL `colorsys.rgb_to_hls`. Same script re-measures the
re-blessed goldens (same demos, same pinned sha base).  |  tools/ci-local.sh:59: "Sprite/palette presence scan (the look-book §2 palette oracle — 7.1)|tools/harness.sh palcheck"
detail: This PR exists because the LEFOU mute shipped through green CI via a golden re-bless. Pixel goldens don't measure saturation; only the ephemeral uncommitted script does, so the same mute can recur undetected.
recommended_fix: Add a palcheck leg measuring top-2% HSL saturation on the dense blessed goldens (juice, estate_surge, growth-88000) with >=0.85 floors; sparse frames get measured floors.

title: router_led token change never renders — sprite path bypasses it and no test exercises the primitive fallback
detail: Spec item 'node accents up (router LEDs)' ships inert: goldens and palcheck pin the baked sprite LED {46,139,87}; the new {0,205,90} renders in no test or golden, so the claim is unverifiable.
recommended_fix: Either re-bake the sprite LEDs to {0,205,90} (art PR, re-bless) or drop the token claim; add a palcheck pin for whichever LED color actually ships.

title: New network tokens unpinned on the fallback_palette/jcol-default copies — only canvas is
detail: fallback_palette and the jcol defaults restate the eight changed tokens by hand (verified in sync this PR); nothing pins their equality with data/palette.json, so a future edit can drift silently.
recommended_fix: One test: fallback_palette() == palette_load() token-by-token, plus a key-stripped-JSON leg for the jcol defaults — pins all three copies together.
